passage.text: Last Sunday, I had dinner with Nam's family at their home in Bangkok.
passage.reading: ˈlæst ˈsʌndeɪ, aɪ ˈhæd ˈdɪnər wɪð ˈnɑːmz ˈfæməli ət ðɛr ˈhoʊm ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk.

passage.text: I was nervous because I didn't want to do anything wrong, but it was a lovely evening.
passage.reading: aɪ wʌz ˈnɜːrvəs bɪˈkɔːz aɪ ˈdɪdənt ˈwɑːnt tə ˈduː ˈɛniθɪŋ ˈrɔːŋ, bʌt ɪt wʌz ə ˈlʌvli ˈiːvnɪŋ.

passage.text: Her mom cooked six different dishes, and her dad kept putting more food on my plate!
passage.reading: hɜːr ˈmɑːm ˈkʊkt ˈsɪks ˈdɪfərənt ˈdɪʃɪz, ənd hɜːr ˈdæd ˈkɛpt ˈpʊtɪŋ ˈmɔːr ˈfuːd ɑːn maɪ ˈpleɪt!

passage.text: I remembered to take off my shoes, and I gave everyone a wai.
passage.reading: aɪ rɪˈmɛmbərd tə ˈteɪk ˈɔːf maɪ ˈʃuːz, ənd aɪ ˈɡeɪv ˈɛvriwʌn ə ˈwaɪ.

passage.text: Fah, Nam's younger sister, said that my wai was perfect.
passage.reading: ˈfɑː, ˈnɑːmz ˈjʌŋɡər ˈsɪstər, ˈsɛd ðæt maɪ ˈwaɪ wʌz ˈpɜːrfɪkt.

passage.text: Then I had an embarrassing moment.
passage.reading: ˈðɛn aɪ ˈhæd ən ɪmˈbærəsɪŋ ˈmoʊmənt.

passage.text: I wanted to pay her mom a compliment, so I tried to say "delicious" in Thai.
passage.reading: aɪ ˈwɑːntɪd tə ˈpeɪ hɜːr ˈmɑːm ə ˈkɑːmpləmənt, soʊ aɪ ˈtraɪd tə ˈseɪ dɪˈlɪʃəs ɪn ˈtaɪ.

passage.text: But I said the wrong word, and everyone laughed!
passage.reading: bʌt aɪ ˈsɛd ðə ˈrɔːŋ ˈwɜːrd, ənd ˈɛvriwʌn ˈlæft!

passage.text: Nam told me that I said the Thai word for "what" instead of "delicious."
passage.reading: ˈnɑːm ˈtoʊld miː ðæt aɪ ˈsɛd ðə ˈtaɪ ˈwɜːrd fər ˈwʌt ɪnˈstɛd əv dɪˈlɪʃəs.

passage.text: Luckily, her parents thought it was funny.
passage.reading: ˈlʌkəli, hɜːr ˈpɛrənts ˈθɔːt ɪt wʌz ˈfʌni.

passage.text: At the end of the evening, they gave me the leftovers to take home.
passage.reading: ət ði ˈɛnd əv ði ˈiːvnɪŋ, ðeɪ ˈɡeɪv miː ðə ˈlɛftoʊvərz tə ˈteɪk ˈhoʊm.

passage.text: In Canada, guests tend to bring food, whereas here the hosts give you food to take home!
passage.reading: ɪn ˈkænədə, ˈɡɛsts ˈtɛnd tə ˈbrɪŋ ˈfuːd, ˌwɛrˈæz ˈhɪr ðə ˈhoʊsts ˈɡɪv juː ˈfuːd tə ˈteɪk ˈhoʊm!

passage.text: I'm eating the leftovers for lunch right now.
passage.reading: aɪm ˈiːtɪŋ ðə ˈlɛftoʊvərz fər ˈlʌntʃ ˈraɪt ˈnaʊ.
